name: Conservatism
summary: Conservatism seeks to preserve inherited institutions, customs and social order, distrusting abstract schemes of reform and utopian blueprints. It values authority, family, property, religion and national attachment, and accepts cautious, gradual change that builds on tradition. Its economic and social emphases vary: traditionalist and paternalist strands defend duty and a social order, while fiscal and liberal strands stress free markets and limited government.
scope: Mainstream Western conservatism: the Burkean core (Reflections on the Revolution in France), Oakeshott's and Scruton's philosophical account, and the contemporary Anglo-American party mainstream of fiscal, social and national conservatism as documented in reference works. It excludes reactionary, fascist and monarchist-restorationist currents, non-Western conservatisms, and Christian democracy as a separate family. Where strands disagree (welfare, trade, abortion), answers lean to the documented majority or are given as 0.

keyFigures.name: Edmund Burke
keyFigures.role: Irish-born statesman and author of Reflections on the Revolution in France, widely seen as the father of modern conservatism

keyFigures.name: Michael Oakeshott
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who described conservatism as a disposition favoring the familiar over the untried

keyFigures.name: Roger Scruton
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who defended authority, family, community and religion as conservative foundations

sources.title: Reflections on the Revolution in France, in The Works of the Right Honourable Edmund Burke (World's Classics, vol. 4)
sources.author: Edmund Burke
sources.usedFor: Burke's defense of inheritance, prescription, property, gradual reform and rejection of abstract rights.

sources.usedFor: Contemporary mainstream positions on taxes, welfare, guns, defense, trade, schooling and deficits.

universal-healthcare.rationale: US conservatives oppose state intervention in healthcare, though British one-nation conservatives accepted the NHS, so this is a weak lean.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Mainstream conservatives prefer market-set wages and deregulation; inferred from their general opposition to market intervention.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Fiscal and liberal conservatism favor limited interference in markets, though traditionalists like Scruton want markets bounded by custom.

public-ownership.rationale: Conservative movements favor privatization and free enterprise over state ownership of industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Conservatives favor low taxes and call higher levies on wealth unjust.

unions-good.rationale: Conservatives are markedly more opposed to labor unions than liberals and social democrats.

property-fundamental.rationale: Burke and later conservatives treat property as a foundation of liberty and social order.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Conservatives generally favor deregulation, though paternalist strands accept some limits on business; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Fiscal conservatives want welfare narrowed while paternalist conservatives defend a safety net grounded in duty, so adherents are split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Conservatives defend ordinary private ownership and capitalism rather than collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Law and order and national security rank high, so security measures are usually tolerated; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Social conservatives support prohibiting drugs, with only libertarian-leaning conservatives dissenting.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Conservatives usually resist speech restrictions as state overreach; inferred, not a central tradition point.

strong-leader.rationale: Conservatism favors restraint of power and settled institutions over leaders who bypass them; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Conservatism treats authority and the state as necessary to social order, the opposite of anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: Conservatives in the US strongly back gun rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: Law and order and strong national defense are standard conservative planks.

decide-locally.rationale: Federalism and local community are valued, though conservatives also defend national institutions.

rehabilitation.rationale: Conservatives emphasize law and order and punishment, though many support rehabilitation programs; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Social conservatives treat the traditional family as society's foundational unit.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social conservatives defend marriage as one man and one woman, although liberal conservatives have accepted reform.

abortion-legal.rationale: Social and religious conservatives oppose abortion; secular and liberal conservatives are a minority.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religious conservatives seek a larger public role for religion; Burke favored an established church, though secular conservatives exist.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Conservatives tend to oppose active state remedies of this kind; inferred from their preference for equal treatment and limited government.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Social conservatives rest their view on traditional sex roles and the family; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Attachment to inherited ways of life, place and nation is central to conservatism.

gradual-change.rationale: Burke held that a state without means of some change lacks the means of its conservation, favoring cautious reform of inherited institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: National conservatives and many European and US conservatives support limiting immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Conservatives stress national sovereignty and often oppose supranational bodies; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Conservatives have varied widely between free trade and protectionism, with a recent tilt to protectionism.

nation-first.rationale: Conservatives emphasize national identity and sovereignty.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Burke distrusted universal abstract claims, but interventionist conservatives exist; inferred and split.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders conflict with conservative emphasis on nation, culture and opposition to immigration.

limit-growth.rationale: Conservatives support capitalism and economic growth and oppose environmental intervention.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Conservatives question climate policy more than liberals and oppose heavy state intervention on the environment.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Conservatives are pessimistic about human nature and skeptical of utopian schemes.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Conservatives favor energy supply and deregulation over environmental limits; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Conservatism accepts gradual reform but rejects sudden, planned or revolutionary change, as Burke did of 1789.

experts-over-public.rationale: Conservatives distrust rationalist technocracy and prize inherited practice over expert blueprints; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Oakeshott's critique of rationalism in politics rejects blueprint planning, and conservatives defend markets.

socialized-markets.rationale: Conservatives favor private enterprise and oppose both state and worker ownership of firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Conservatives want lower taxes and defend property; this radical single-tax scheme is not part of the tradition.

tax-inheritance.rationale: US conservatives oppose the estate tax, which they call a death tax, and inheritance fits their view of property and family.

basic-income.rationale: Conservatives prefer limited, narrowly tailored welfare; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The right has split between free trade and protectionism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Conservatives oppose state direction of the economy in favor of markets.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Burke prized property but defended landed aristocratic holdings, and modern conservatives defend corporations too, so adherents split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Conservatism defends capitalism and property, the opposite of this communist goal.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Mainstream conservatives accept established monetary institutions; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Conservative corporatism exists in places such as Japan, but mainstream Anglo-American conservatives favor market bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: Conservatism values established institutions and is compatible with democracy, not ideological single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Traditional conservatives defended monarchy as an inherited institution and some still do.

democracy-best.rationale: The SEP says conservatism is not essentially opposed to democracy, though it values constraint on popular will; inferred.

direct-votes.rationale: Conservatives favor representative and institutional government over direct popular rule; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is a socialist model foreign to conservatives, who defend existing parliamentary institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: Attachment to inherited national communities and institutions disfavors secession; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Conservatives accept natural distinctions and hierarchy as part of social order.

political-violence-never.rationale: Conservatives reject revolution but accept force by lawful authority, so an absolute ban is not their line.

war-builds-character.rationale: Prudence and stability are conservative watchwords, though militarism appears in some strands; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Many conservatives want cooperation between church and state, though secular conservatives exist.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mainstream conservatives want laws informed by religion and natural law, with only a minority seeking scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Law and order and strong state defense are core conservative positions.

military-superiority.rationale: Conservatives support a strong military and peace through strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Mainstream conservatism stresses cultural and civic national identity; ethnic nationalism is a fringe; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Conservatives treat society as an organic whole with mutual duties, not defined by class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Conservatives accept inequality and hierarchy as natural parts of social order.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not a central issue; inferred from conservative emphasis on property rights and national sovereignty.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Conservatives generally oppose such redistributive claims; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Conservatives stress particular nations over supranational union; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Conservatives ground order in duty, family and religion rather than self-interest, despite market support; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Burke rejected abstract rights and conservatives root rights in tradition and duty to community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Green conservatism exists but many conservatives resist environmental limits, so this is split; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Pro-family and natalist conservatives oppose active limits on population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Conservatives defend capitalism and the existing civilization.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Conservatives prefer stability and the familiar to disruptive change to institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Skepticism of utopian projects and attachment to inherited norms suggests wariness; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: This is rationalist blueprint rule of the kind Oakeshott opposed; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Conservatives split between liberty and law-and-order concerns; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The SEP says conservatives value stability over improvement; whether to restore a lost order splits them.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Oakeshott described conservatism as a disposition, not a doctrine, preferring the practical and tried to blueprints.

direct-action.rationale: Conservatives favor change through established institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not a conservative theme; inferred as indifferent.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Conservatism values inherited civilization, property and institutions.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A communist aim that conservatives reject, defending capitalism and property.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Conservatives accept inequality and property and reject this communist principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Conservatives defend capitalism and free enterprise, including the profit motive.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Conservatives defend capitalism and reject the Marxist labor theory of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Conservatism opposes revolution and class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Conservatives defend private and family property.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Conservatives defend capitalism and reject this Marxist-Leninist claim.

taxation-theft.rationale: US conservatives hold that unnecessary taxation is unjust, but accept the state and its taxing power.

harm-principle.rationale: Social conservatives support restricting drugs, prostitution and pornography beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Burke rejected abstract individual rights; conservatives root rights in inherited tradition and community.

conscription.rationale: Conservatives split between favoring national service and distrusting state coercion; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Conservatives value attachment to place and nation and accept political institutions; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Conservatives see the state as an inherited community, not a firm, even when favoring efficiency; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Contemporary conservatives often make this complaint, but none of the sources opened states it directly; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Mainstream conservatism does not take this position; it appears only in fringe strands.

organic-representation.rationale: Organic society is a conservative theme, but mainstream conservatives work through parties; inferred and split.

total-state.rationale: Conservatives favor limited government and civil society against rationalist total direction.

national-rebirth.rationale: Conservatives prefer the familiar and gradual repair to radical rebirth, which is fascist rhetoric.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Conservatives stress prudence and defense of the existing nation; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Burke defended inherited institutions but within a constitutional order, not feudal personal oaths; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Conservatives defend free property and free enterprise, not bondage.

universal-morality.rationale: Natural law conservatives affirm universal moral order, while Burke distrusted abstract reason and universal claims.

single-common-good.rationale: Oakeshott and Burke oppose politics driven by a rational blueprint; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Israeli conservatism supports a Jewish state and many Western conservatives back Israel; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Conservatives stress national belonging but have no common position on diaspora return; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Conservatives value national culture, but language revival is case specific; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Conservatives defend owner and management control of firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: US conservatives support school choice and vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal conservatives support balanced budgets and reduced debt.

economic-freedom.rationale: Burke and later conservatives link liberty to property, though traditionalists qualify market doctrine.

rule-by-example.rationale: Conservatives value virtue and example but also rule of law and authority; inferred and split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Conservatives stress national identity and sovereignty, so they favor a people governing itself in its own state, though they stress inherited, existing states over new ones.

force-without-un.rationale: Mainstream Anglo-American conservatives stress national sovereignty and national interest over international approval, though some traditionalists favour caution; inferred from the sovereignty and defense emphasis in the contemporary party mainstream.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Conservatism is skeptical of rationalism in politics and values religion, tradition and inherited prejudice as guides, though modern fiscal conservatives lean more on evidence, so the disagreement is moderate.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: National and US conservatives commonly favor restricting benefits for non-citizens, though paternalist and liberal strands are less firm; inferred from the mainstream stance on immigration.

positive-liberty.rationale: Conservatives usually stress freedom as ordered liberty and personal responsibility rather than material provision; inferred from US conservative positions against expansive welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Mainstream US and UK conservatives back work requirements for able-bodied benefit recipients, as in the 1996 welfare reform.

class-collaboration.rationale: Conservatives hold an organic view of society where ranks cooperate, and reject class struggle; Burke and the SEP stress social harmony and hierarchy.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving inherited institutions is the defining conservative aim; Burke defended prescription and inheritance against sweeping away the old.

dominated-front.rationale: Mainstream Western conservatives favour alliances with Western powers and national interest, not fronts against them; inferred from US conservative defence and foreign policy.

workers-nation.rationale: Conservatives reject international class organization but also do not call for class organization at all, favouring national unity across classes; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditionalist conservatives defend traditional sex roles but mainstream parties accept legal equality, so adherents are split.

ban-interest.rationale: Conservatives defend property, contract and capital markets, and no mainstream conservatism seeks to ban interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Mainstream conservatism in the contemporary West rejects legal racial segregation; this excludes reactionary currents as the audit scope states.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Conservatives see the state as an inherited institution of order and authority serving society as a whole, not a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred: the contemporary Anglo-American conservative mainstream, especially in the US, favours expanding domestic energy output.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Conservatism values national attachment and shared custom, and the mainstream expects immigrants to adopt national culture; strands differ. Inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: The mainstream rejects this claim, held by populist and far-right currents that the scope excludes.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Anglo-American mainstream defends district-based systems for stable, accountable government; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Burke opposed exporting a political system by force or doctrine; neoconservatives dissent, so this is a weak lean.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Conservatives generally hold that sex differences are natural and long-standing institutions are not systematically unjust; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Split: populist conservatives say yes, while Burkean conservatives trust established elites and institutions.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics found support among some early conservatives, but the modern mainstream, with its emphasis on family and religion, rejects it; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Mainstream conservatives are wary of retrospective prosecution of soldiers and police and prefer to leave old abuses to domestic institutions; inferred, and strands differ.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mainstream conservatism accepts more than a minimal state, including social functions, though fiscal conservatives lean toward limits.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mainstream conservatives do not usually favour legal or social discouragement of interracial marriage, though some traditionalists value same-group family life.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mainstream conservatives accept equal rights before the law, but the Burkean tradition also accepts social hierarchy, so the agreement is weak.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Mainstream conservatism rejects socialism altogether and does not address its survival; inferred only.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from the national attachment and respect for established states that mainstream conservatives hold; adherents vary.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Conservatives are split between a common law for all citizens and respect for inherited religious and communal custom.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Many conservatives favour curbing coercive conversion in the name of religious tradition, but mainstream Western conservatives mostly accept religious freedom.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from respect for religious custom, though Western mainstream conservatives rarely propose such bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: US conservatives commonly support school prayer and religious teaching in public schools, and conservatism values religion in public life.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred from conservative preference for limited government, though conservatives value strong defense; the statement concerns socialist states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Burke rejected the idea that authority rests on an original contract or abstract popular consent, resting it on prescription and tradition.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: conservatives treat tradition and settled institutions as accumulated wisdom and distrust the claim that knowledge merely masks power.

trade-surplus.rationale: Adherents are split between free-trade fiscal conservatives and protectionist or economic-nationalist strands.

population-transfer.rationale: Mainstream conservatism upholds rule of law and property and does not endorse expelling minorities, though some national strands tolerate pressure.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Conservatives accept state coercion for order, defense and law, so the ban on initiating force is not absolute; inferred from Burke and the order tradition.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fiscal and market strands credit competition, while traditionalist strands stress duty, community and inherited institutions.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on preserving the constitutional order and authority; many conservatives accept banning parties that aim to destroy it.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Burke condemns arbitrary power yet conservatives speak of ordered liberty under law rather than non-domination; adherents are split.

separated-powers.rationale: Burke defends a balanced constitution, and US conservatism stresses constitutional limits and divided government.

vanguard-party.rationale: Burke rejects revolutionary movements, and conservatism opposes vanguard-led transformation of society.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Conservatives generally favor equal treatment under law and limited welfare; paternalist strands dissent, so this is a lean.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Right to buy was a flagship Thatcher-era conservative policy, spreading property ownership.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Mainstream conservatives favour legal limits such as strike ballots, inferred from the party mainstream.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian arguments appear in some strands; modern mainstream conservatives are split, so the answer is inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Conservative attachment to shared culture and national tradition leans this way, but the mainstream strand accepts diversity; adherents split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Burke and Scruton defend inherited order and established institutions; chance selection runs against prescription and ability.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Conservatives value order and security but also limited government and rule of law; strands split, so this is inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Market-oriented conservatives oppose price ceilings, though paternalist strands accept them in crises; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mainstream conservatives defend a free press, although some favour state broadcasting rules; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Conservatism upholds constitutional order and a state-controlled army, not party command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Conservatives favour integration and longer residence for citizenship, inferred from the immigration stance in reference works.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Conservatives value established institutions and reward for service, and do not favor leveling officials to a worker's wage; inferred from general principles.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Burke held that representatives owe their judgment, not obedience, to those who choose them, an inference applied to party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: National attachment and distrust of abstract schemes lead conservatives to keep sovereignty, with the EU a common target of mainstream conservative criticism.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Conservatives split: constitutional conservatives favor legislative checks while monarchist and presidential traditions favor executive command; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Conservatives value religion and hierarchy, and episcopal churches such as the Anglican are an established conservative institution; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Conservatives respect religion's role but mainstream Western conservatism does not seek clerical government; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Loyalty to nation and its institutions is central, so mainstream conservatives reject working for one's own country's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Traditionalist conservatives accept restrictions on obscene or corrupting art, while fiscal and liberal conservatives resist; a weak lean, inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Mainstream US conservatives backed the 22nd Amendment and term limits, and Burke distrusted concentrated power; inferred as a weak lean.

recall-officials.rationale: Burke's view that representatives exercise judgment and offices be stable implies caution about recall; inferred, with US conservatives split on it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Mainstream conservatives generally back alliances such as NATO, though a nationalist strand dissents; inferred from party practice.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Conservatives defend property and market arrangements, and Burke defended property against leveling; abolishing rent is inferred to be rejected.

people-in-arms.rationale: American conservatives defend gun rights, but mainstream conservatism supports professional armies and national defense; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Conservatives have long idealised rural and agrarian life and the country gentry; inferred, with a milder view among modern urban conservatives.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Conservatives support national unity but prize stability and existing borders; adherents are split and the sources do not address the case.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Modern conservatives, especially in the US, often criticise academic elites; Burke likewise distrusted abstract theorising intellectuals. This is documented but not core.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Conservatives tend to hold that their own inherited civilization has particular worth and reject relativism; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The US conservative mainstream and many conservative parties support capital punishment for the gravest crimes.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Social conservatives often oppose or limit school sex and gender education and favor parental control; inferred from the US conservative movement.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious conservatives in the US push for teaching creationism, but the wider tradition does not, so adherents are split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatives favor legal limits on pornography, though libertarian-leaning conservatives dissent; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Conservatives and national conservatives favor tighter citizenship rules, but the US conservative mainstream defends birthright citizenship; inferred and split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Conservatives tend to favor a common national language and less state support for multilingual services; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Conservatives, especially in the US, defend religious liberty exemptions, yet the tradition also values uniform law and an established religion; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conservatives value custom and social convention, and Burke held that prejudice and prescription are useful; inferred to reject encouraging nonconformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Mainstream conservatives treat debts as obligations to be honoured and favour fiscal discipline; inferred from their stance on deficits.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Conservatives distrust schemes to transform the economic order and value inherited institutions, so they hold independence worthwhile on its own; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Burke attacked the French National Assembly for remaking the constitution from abstract principles and held that change should build on inherited institutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Conservatives value order and authority but tie liberty to inherited law and do not make it a price for growth; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Conservatives stress duties to family and nation first and treat foreign aid as discretionary; inferred from national attachment.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Mainstream conservatives favour strong national defence and sovereignty, which usually supports a national deterrent; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Conservatives split between defending hereditary or parliamentary heads of state and direct election, as in the US; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Conservatives favour sound money and fiscal discipline and generally accept independent price-stability central banks; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: National attachment pulls against ceding territory but conservative governments have made such deals, so adherents are split; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Burke and traditionalists see property as an inherited trust with duties, while fiscal conservatives defend owners' freedom to use it; strands split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Conservatives usually call the USSR a totalitarian socialist state, not state capitalist; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Burkean caution about change favors prudence, but US conservatives often resist environmental regulation on uncertain risk, so adherents split.

collective-defense.rationale: The mainstream Anglo-American conservative party line backs NATO-style alliances and strong defense, inferred from its defense positions.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from conservative respect for law, national sovereignty and borders; mainstream conservatives condemn conquest, though realist strands accept established control.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Burke condemned the confiscation of church estates and called it sacrilege, and conservatives value religion as a pillar of social order.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Burkean conservatism defends hereditary monarchy and institutions as symbols of continuity, and the crown stands above party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the conservative emphasis on national unity, order and inherited institutions; the US conservative mainstream accepts Union victory.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Conservatives value local custom and federalism but also national unity, and the ideology has no settled view on special autonomy arrangements.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Burke defended monarchy as inherited, but on law and custom rather than divine descent; the mainstream strand is secular, with only a traditionalist fringe holding divine right.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Fiscal conservatives and the US mainstream favor low, simple taxes and have promoted flat-tax proposals, though not all agree.

character-from-environment.rationale: The SEP notes conservative skepticism of rationalist social engineering and belief in human imperfection and fixed nature, against the view that circumstances can remake people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Burke and the conservative tradition stress prescription and constitutional limits, with rulers bound by inherited law.

space-expansion.rationale: No conservative doctrine on space; national-prestige and fiscal-restraint arguments pull in opposite directions.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Burke praised the balance of crown, lords and commons in the British constitution and distrusted pure democracy.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from conservative distrust of charismatic politics and reverence for institutions over persons; honours to monarchs are tradition, not leader worship.

equal-parenting.rationale: Conservatives support the family but are split between fathers' rights and traditional custody norms.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from the SEP account of organic society and hierarchy, which rejects class-war doctrine.

land-redistribution.rationale: Burke defends property and inheritance against schemes of leveling.

refugee-return.rationale: Conservatives divide on this issue and doctrine is silent; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Conservatives value national attachment, but also existing order and law; inferred from the SEP account.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religion is valued, but mainstream Western conservatives do not back legal penalties for leaving it; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mainstream Western conservatism favours limited government and does not back dress mandates; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Sovereignty-minded Anglo-American conservatives tend to oppose shared currencies; inferred, and continental conservatives differ.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from attachment to existing nations and inherited institutions over cross-border projects.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: No settled conservative doctrine; split between assimilationist and pluralist conservatives.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from respect for the existing state and its law and institutions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The SEP account stresses tradition, religion and manners as shaping society, against materialist theories.

ban-cartels.rationale: Conservatives split between free-market antitrust and tolerance of business concentration.

no-bailouts.rationale: Fiscal conservatives oppose bailouts, but the mainstream has backed them in crises; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Burke prized prescription and balanced institutions, but US conservatives also back judicial constraints; inferred lean.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Mainstream conservatives oppose quotas and mandated parity; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Mainstream conservatives favour trade or economic nationalism but not closed blocs; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Contemporary conservatives oppose binding standards in trade deals as regulation and cost; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Duty is a conservative value, but replacing incentives is a utopian scheme of the kind it distrusts.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Burke treats revolution as destructive and favours gradual reform within inherited institutions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Burke defended a mitigated nobility, but modern conservatives mostly accept existing arrangements without insisting on titles; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Conservatives stress national attachment and inherited tradition, and US conservatives back history teaching centred on the national story.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Burkean prudence and anti-utopianism cut against imposed improvement, but older imperial conservatism defended it, so adherents split; inferred from the strands.

patriotic-education.rationale: National attachment is a core conservative value and mainstream conservatives favour teaching patriotism in schools.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Contemporary Anglo-American conservatives broadly oppose race-conscious admissions and hiring in favour of colour-blind treatment.

public-money-creation.rationale: Mainstream conservatives accept the existing banking and central-bank system and distrust state-directed monetary schemes; inferred from this.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Mainstream conservatives defend market economies as resilient and reject collapse theories; inferred from their economic emphases.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed by the Burkean core; national conservatives may favour such ties while others do not, so adherents split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Conservative strands favour trade and market integration, and delinking is a radical scheme conservatives distrust.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Conservatives reject the Marxist class framework of exploiters and exploited, and the labour-aristocracy thesis in particular; inferred from this.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Property rights matter to conservatives, but most mainstream conservatives accept anti-discrimination law; fiscal-liberal strands lean the other way.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: US conservatives champion the entrenched Constitution and Bill of Rights, though Burke preferred inherited custom to written abstract rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Burkean respect for prescription and inherited arrangements suggests existing treaties and borders stand; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Burke defended hereditary succession as part of the inherited constitution, though modern conservatives largely accept elected heads of government.

minority-veto.rationale: Conservatives value order and authority; a binding veto for any individual dissenter would dissolve collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Burke justified the 1688 Revolution as a last resort when the king broke the constitution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Burkean conservatism supports the English constitution of King-in-Parliament, with Parliament as the effective lawmaker.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: mainstream conservatives accept animal cruelty laws, but doctrine is silent.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the property and tradition emphasis, including farming and hunting.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist and one-nation conservatism hold that privilege brings duties to the less fortunate, and Burke defends a natural aristocracy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Oakeshott and others value private life, but conservatism teaches duty and service to the community; inferred mild rejection.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Conservatives criticise mass culture's coarsening of taste but not as a tool that reproduces the social order; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim outside conservatism; Burke does stress custom and opinion as supports of authority; split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mainstream conservatives defend free trade and market development and reject dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: National conservatives favour citizen preference while liberal conservatives hold to equal citizenship; split.

party-own-road.rationale: A question internal to communist parties; no position follows.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Mainstream US conservatives are sceptical of foreign aid and favour trade and investment; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Conservatives value order and the existing settlement, though nationalist strands support irredentism; inferred mild rejection.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Conservatives hold to equal citizenship and oppose group-based political privilege.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Post-war conservative parties in Germany and Italy accept it, while others reject it as a partisan test; split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Mainstream conservatives explicitly condemn fascism and communism together as totalitarian.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Historical consensus holds slavery was the main cause; some US conservatives emphasise states' rights, so the rejection is moderate.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Defending inherited symbols and heritage is characteristic of conservatism and of contemporary US conservatives.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from conservative concern with men's role in the family and the culture, though it is not a doctrinal point.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by doctrine; adherents split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Burke argues institutions grow from a people's history and cannot be imposed by abstract schemes.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Mainstream Western conservatism holds civilian control of the military; reactionary currents that favour a political army are outside scope.

paid-care-work.rationale: Conservatives value the family's unpaid caring role but resist new state payment; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Conservatives value the family and inherited duties between generations, though they do not make lifelong support a doctrine.

office-by-exam.rationale: Burke defends a natural aristocracy but the Anglo-American mainstream uses election and appointment; adherents are not united on examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Fiscal conservatives favour open markets while national conservatives favour blocking takeovers, so the strands divide.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Social conservatives defend marriage as an institution and resist easy divorce, though liberal strands accept it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Burke held that representatives owe their judgment rather than obedience to instructions, so binding and recalling them is rejected.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Contemporary American conservatives favour private pension accounts, though European conservatives accept state schemes.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Secure private property is central to Burkean and mainstream conservatism, which rejects community land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Legislative control of the purse is part of the constitutional order that conservatives defend.

single-official-language.rationale: National attachment leads many conservatives, notably in the US, to favour a common official language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Adherents are split between property-rights and national-conservative strands.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Mainstream American conservatism holds that discrimination means intentional treatment, not unequal outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Traditionalists criticise materialism while market conservatives defend consumer choice, so the strands divide.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anglo-American conservatives backed anti-communist insurgents in the Reagan era, inferred as a majority-leaning view.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Conservatives value alliances and sovereignty, so forced intervention in an ally is inferred as disfavoured.

corporate-influence.rationale: Populist conservatives say yes while fiscal conservatives deny it, so adherents divide.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: National conservatives stress sovereignty against outside influence; inferred, contested among free-market strands.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Family-centered conservatism supports pro-family policy and often prefers it to immigration; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Burke defended property rights, which cut against restricting who may buy, though local community appeals to some.

job-guarantee.rationale: Mainstream conservatives oppose state job schemes and favor market employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Burke distrusted abstract schemes like exporting democracy; inferred from that skepticism.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Conservatism values authority and law as inherited order, not as optional.

non-intervention.rationale: Conservatives defend sovereignty, but many back military action; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Mainstream conservatives are wary of union power; industry versus craft is not addressed, so inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream conservatism rejects blaming a minority; conspiracy beliefs belong to fringe strands.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Scruton and the tradition treat marriage and family as foundational institutions.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Conservatives value order and secrecy for security, but also limited government; split.

local-production.rationale: Conservatives favor free trade, so a preference for local production is inferred as disfavored.

informal-organisation.rationale: Burke valued established institutions and distrusted informal, unaccountable groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Mainstream conservatives defend national sovereignty over international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Religion is valued as a foundation of social order, but strands differ on defining the nation by it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Conservative national sovereignty and strong defense favor independence over submission; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Conservatives value local government but also national unity and fiscal responsibility; adherents split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Conservatism defends private property including productive property against common ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: Mainstream US and Western conservatives were strongly anti-communist, favoring victory in the Cold War.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Contemporary conservatives favor school choice and private providers, and the statement allows public funding; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion is a core value of conservatism, so it is not regarded as illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Conservatives value capitalism and credit it with prosperity; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Conservatives reject economic transformation as utopian; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: The family is a core conservative institution and socializing care is opposed; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Conservative nationalists favor language preservation but others find purging impractical; adherents split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Burke defends inherited rights and prescription, including binding compacts; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Conservatism rejects utopian reorganization into communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Mainstream conservatism favors integration but not state-led settlement; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Mainstream conservatives defend capitalism as sound; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Inherited institutions and customs deserve respect even when their reasons are not fully understood.
missingStatements.rationale: Burke defended prescription and inheritance against abstract reasoning, and Oakeshott preferred the tried to the untried.

missingStatements.text: Existing property and social ranks should be defended against schemes of radical leveling.
missingStatements.rationale: Burke's Reflections defends property and a mitigated nobility, and the SEP notes acceptance of hierarchy.

notes: Strands differ: paternalist one-nation conservatives accept welfare and the NHS, fiscal conservatives and US movement conservatives favor free markets and low taxes, and national conservatives stress immigration limits and protection. Recent trends shifted much of the right toward protectionism. Many economic and technology answers are inferred, since Burke and Oakeshott did not address them.
